newsitem.title: CANADA: Repap rallies on sale of U.S. operations.
newsitem.headline: Repap rallies on sale of U.S. operations.

text.p: Repap Enterprises Inc shares rallied on Wednesday after the company said it agreed to sell its U.S. operations to Consolidated Papers Inc for US$674 million.
Repap shares rose 0.13 to 0.51 on the Toronto Stock Exchang from its 52-week low of 0.38 on volume of more than 1 million shares. The stock's 52-week high was 5.80.

Analyst Brian Topp of BZW Canada said Repap appeared to get a good price for its Repap USA unit, which comprises the Montreal-based company's coated paper production, sales and distribution operations in Wisconsin.
"I was pleasantly surprised by how much money they got. It was certainly in excess of what I thought they would receive," Topp said.
Repap said it also agreed to sell its kraft paper and lumber operations in The Pas, Manitoba, to Tolko Industries Ltd, a closely-held company based in British Columbia, for an undisclosed amount.

Repap said it intended to continue operating its 492,000-ton New Brunswick coated paper, market pulp and lumber operations. The company said it planned to reduce costs by more than C$20 million at its New Brunswick operations in 1997.
Topp said that despite the rally in Repap's share price, the investment community would find it difficult to get enthusiastic about heavily indebted Repap's prospects.
"It's hard to get overly excited about this company. It's now a one mill company," Topp said.
Repap said net proceed from the sale of Repap USA would be used to reduce liabilities at the parent company level.

At April 30, Repap had consolidated debt of C$2.3 billion. About C$270 million of debt owed to two Canadian banks and another lender is due July 28. Repap also has US$130 million of convertible debentures maturing on August 1.
